title: Eisenstein ideal and rational torsion of modular Jacobians
summary: Prime-level Eisenstein arithmetic of modular Jacobians, from integral weight-two congruences and the cuspidal class through component groups, finite-flat Galois modules, local Hecke rings, Ogg’s rational torsion theorem and descent. The Eisenstein quotient is an abelian variety and its rational points are the image of the cuspidal subgroup. The final prime-torsion classification includes all primes, with a separate level-13 descent.
readme: Develop the full prime-level Eisenstein ideal and its actual abelian quotient, the exact cuspidal and Shimura subgroup schemes, the component group at the level prime, odd and dyadic multiplicity one, winding maps, Ogg’s rational torsion theorem and global cohomological descent. The resulting finite rational group of the Eisenstein quotient drives the modular-cusp descent for prime torsion, with the separate Mazur–Tate level 13 argument. Cusp specialization is stated for the level subgroup on generalized elliptic curves; the j-valuation rule is its corollary. The reader document specifies all hypotheses, APIs, Checks, supplier contracts and arithmetic certificates.

stages.title: Integral Eisenstein arithmetic
stages.description: Fix n, the full integral Eisenstein eigensystem and its kernel, distinguish its image I in the cuspidal Hecke ring T, prove the weight-two integral congruence criterion and T/I ≅ Z/n. These statements include the zero Jacobian cases.

stages.title: Cusps, components and the Shimura subgroup
stages.description: Construct the cuspidal subgroup and Shimura subgroup, compute the rational component group at P from the regular modular curve, prove the exact cuspidal order and Néron specialization splitting, and separate their odd and dyadic intersections.

stages.title: Eisenstein kernels and abelian quotients
stages.description: Define Néron closures of ideal torsion, the completed Eisenstein local rings and the ideal-supported abelian quotient. Prove the quotient’s support and functoriality, with no quotient by IJ substituted for the Eisenstein abelian variety.

stages.title: Odd Eisenstein torsion and multiplicity one
stages.description: Identify Eisenstein residual constituents and their admissible integral models, prove the local étale multiplicity statement, define good auxiliary primes, and establish the odd-primary structure, maximal ideal generators and Gorenstein property.

stages.title: Dyadic torsion and winding homomorphisms
stages.description: Embed the exceptional finite-flat group D at dyadic Eisenstein primes, prove its separation from the plus factor, establish dyadic multiplicity one and the minus quotient, then construct the winding homomorphism and prove local principality for every Eisenstein prime. Include the quadratic modular unit with its corrected Fricke relation and the normalized modular-symbol winding congruence.

stages.title: Ogg’s rational torsion theorem
stages.description: Prove Eisenstein support of rational torsion in arbitrary modular quotients, identify J0(P)(Q)tors with the cuspidal subgroup, prove maximality of the Shimura μ-type subgroup and compare torsion under the minus and Eisenstein quotient maps.

stages.title: Global descent and the Eisenstein quotient
stages.description: Apply the global admissible-group cohomology inequality to the connected Néron kernels, prove bounded fppf H¹ and finite localized Mordell–Weil modules, deduce A_Eis(Q)≅Z/n, and obtain finiteness of X0(P)(Q) in positive genus. Record the Eisenstein-primary Tate–Shafarevich consequence.

stages.title: Cusp moduli and prime-torsion descent
stages.description: Relate degenerating cyclic subgroups to the two cusps using generalized elliptic curves, derive the j-valuation rule, prove the global component-escape step via odd good-reduction specialization of the Eisenstein quotient, and finish the prime-torsion exclusion for every positive-genus prime level. Include the formal-immersion alternative with its ramification hypothesis.

stages.title: Level thirteen and all prime orders
stages.description: Treat the remaining genus-zero level 13 through the genus-two curve X1(13), its order 19 descent and the twisted diamond action. Give the occurring prime orders2,3,5,7 and the all-prime exclusion theorem. Export only the residual invariant-vector consequence that rational point torsion actually proves.
